text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000041 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but only 5 charts came back, too few to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is concerning. The excess 99215 share holds at every complexity level, not just among sicker patients. Most 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and sampled examples carry simple diagnoses such as UTI (C0017213, C0017223), upper respiratory infection (C0017168) and follow-up-only Z09 (C0017190, C0017388). The documentation cannot settle it: the 2 documented 99215s (C0017077, C0017242) both support high MDM, but that is far too few charts to weigh against the 14% all-provider unsupported rate, and the one note claiming moderate-plus data review with no lab line is only weak evidence of inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the zero-condition acute-diagnosis visits, to see whether high MDM is genuinely documented or templated."}
